body:
Actually, Linear should be used for EXR files and other HDR file formats that have their texture data linear-encoded and sRGB should be used for file formats that store their texture data as sRGB-encoded, like SDR PNG, JPG, etc.

To be honest, I don’t even know the full list of which file formats need to use which one. It will take more research and trial and error to determine this. You can use the [test files](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120222#issuecomment-4762695381) I provided as `Sprite` nodes and remap luminance to r, g, and b channels to view the luminance via the Sprite. Notice that EXR needs to use linear and PNG needs to use sRGB to get consistent and correct behaviour.

To me, this API is not suitable for merging because it is too complicated for the average user and requires deep understanding of the engine internals to use correctly. A better API would be to simply have a single “luminance” remap option that automatically and correctly calculates the luminance.

@Calinou 

>This should describe when to use one mode over the other. As I understand it, Linear should be used for textures that will be displayed in 3D, while sRGB should be used for textures that will be displayed in 2D.

Frankly, it's hard for me to say myself. I provided both options because that's extensive enough to cover all cases that might realistically happen, not because I know which is the "correct" one for every branch of engine execution ATM :D

Allen is prolly right here though:

> Linear should be used for EXR files and other HDR file formats that have their texture data linear-encoded and sRGB should be used for file formats that store their texture data as sRGB-encoded, like SDR PNG, JPG, etc.

>To me, this API is not suitable for merging because it is too complicated for the average user and requires deep understanding of the engine internals to use correctly. A better API would be to simply have a single “luminance” remap option that automatically and correctly calculates the luminance.

Sure, it would be better. If you know how to realistically automatically determine if an image is having sRGB or linear data, tell me how. I knew how to do it in 3.x (code was suboptimal but existed), I haven't a slightest idea in 4.x unless I would re-implement the removed 3.x code (scanning PNGs for headers while loading etc.). 

That said, is it an API at all? Not every single line of engine code is an API, not everything should be assumed to be programatically exposed. It's a front-facing UI component for a subfeature of a rarely-used functionality; channel remapping is not a function that is used by "the average user" at all.
